text.p: Highlands Gold Ltd said on Thursday that pre-feasability studies at the group's Ramu and Frieda River projects in Papua New Guinea had shown both could be developed into viable mines within a decade.

"The Ramu (nickel-cobalt) and Frieda River (copper-gold) pre-feasability studies demonstrate the two projects have the potential to be developed into viable mines within the decade," managing director Ian Goddard said in the annual report.
Highlands and its Japanese joint venturer, OMRD Frieda Co Ltd, were seeking a third party to enter the Frieda River project, Goddard said.
At Ramu, the group's Nord Pacific Ltd joint venturer was also helping in seeking a third party to fund a bankable feasability study, Goddard said.
"We are pleased and encouraged that a number of large international mining and processing companies has approached us for information with respect to these joint venture opportunities," he said.
